wstep: This card follows the citric-acid mozzarella recipe of the UCCE Master Food Preservers of Amador/Calaveras County, adapted from University of Alaska Fairbanks Extension FNH-00063.

akapity: Make this cheese only from pasteurized milk; raw milk must be pasteurized before it is used for cheese.
Do not pasteurize raw milk in a microwave oven, because it does not heat the milk evenly.
The recipe does not give a total making time, so this card does not promise a quick cheese; do not shorten any step to save time.
UCCE uses 1 gallon of milk that is not ultra-pasteurized, because ultra-pasteurized milk does not separate into curds and whey.
Dissolve 1 1/2 teaspoons of citric acid in 1 cup of cool, chlorine-free water.
Dissolve 1/4 rennet tablet or 1/4 teaspoon of liquid rennet in 1/4 cup of cool, chlorine-free water.
You can add 1 teaspoon of cheese salt, or leave it out.
Pour the citric acid solution into the pot, add the milk and stir gently.
Heat the milk slowly to 90 °F (about 32 °C) while stirring.
Take the pot off the heat and fold in the rennet solution, top to bottom, for about 30 seconds.
Cover the pot and leave it undisturbed for 5 minutes.
Cut the curd in a 1-inch (2.5 cm) checkerboard pattern.
Put the pot back on the heat and warm the curd to 105 °F (about 41 °C), stirring slowly and gently.
Take it off the heat and keep stirring slowly for 2–5 minutes.
Move the curd with a slotted spoon to a colander over a bowl and add 3/4–1 teaspoon of salt.
Heat two-thirds of the whey to 175 °F (about 79 °C).
The whey is very hot, so dip the curd into it with the slotted spoon or heat-resistant gloves.
Keep the whey at 170–175 °F (about 77–79 °C), and work, fold and stretch the curd until it is smooth and shiny.
Shape the cheese into balls and cool them in ice water.
Keep the cheese in an airtight container or wrapped in plastic wrap in the refrigerator and eat it within a week, or freeze it for up to a month.
Pregnant women should avoid cheeses made from unpasteurized milk.
